text.p: SME - Herbert Boesch, chairman of the joint Slovak- European Union parliamentary committee, said the recent withdrawal of a mandate of a former deputy of the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) was unacceptable contradicts the proclaimed goal of building democracy.
- Boesch has warned that this trend can have significant negative impact on Slovak chances for integration into the European Union.

- Pavol Bezak, vice-president of major shoe producer CEBO Holding Slovakia a.s. (CHS), was shot dead on Friday. Bezak is the second CHS top executive killed this year, after an unknown assailant shot dead President Anton Jasik in February.
- People in Partizanske, the CHS headquarters, say they believe that Bezak was killed by Russian mafia.
- The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) said it would not support a controversial amendment to the penal code, presented by ruling coalition.
- Opposition parties say that Slovakia is in danger of having its association agreement with the European Union withdrawn.
NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik on Sunday left for a two-day official visit to Russia. Hamzik will meet his counterpart Yevgeny Primakov on Monday.
- Slovak and Czech Prime Ministers Vladimir Meciar and Vaclav Klaus have agreed on a meeting of their finance ministers in the near future to discuss mutual trade relations.
- Printing company Nitrianske Tlaciarne a.s. has signed a one-year contract worth 4.8 million marks with several German publishing houses.

PRAVDA - According to a poll by the independent agency Focus, Meciar's HZDS would have won some 24.4 percent if the an election had been held in November. The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) would have had 13.2 percent, Democratic Union (DU) 11.4 percent and SDL 8.8 percent. About 19 percent of those polled said they would not have voted.
